mechanism_narrative: A higher current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly increases discount rates for equity valuation, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as capital costs rise above earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% over a 5-year walk-forward window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% signals labor market tightness that accelerates consumer spending, generating positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When UNRATE < 3.5%, 5-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year rolling period.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates collapsing consumer demand, triggering negative 60-day S&P 500 returns through reduced corporate revenue forecasts.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS decline in the past 3 months
failure_condition: When HOUST and RSAFS both decline, 60-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: In monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and INDPRO < 95.0), industrial output contraction reduces corporate margins, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 95.0 and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%, 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts level (HOUST) above 1300.0 thousand units reflects robust residential construction, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 returns through related sector growth.
failure_condition: When HOUST > 1300.0, 5-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over a 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL exceeding 315.0 indicates accelerating inflation that forces central bank rate hikes, causing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns via reduced equity attractiveness.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 315.0, 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in employment (PAYEMS) and rise in unemployment (UNRATE) signals labor market deterioration that weakens consumer spending, causing negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises in the past 3 months
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, 60-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of cases over 5 years.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth rate > 3.0% annualized), GDP momentum boosts corporate earnings, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 growth rate > 3.0% annualized, 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of cases over 5 years.
